title: Westland's new lots need a €6 million bank guarantee, and the largest Alder has ever posted was €3.8 million.
status: draft, not checked by a person
sources: Alder annual reports 2021 to 2025; Westland tender notice of 3 October 2026 and general conditions of January 2024; the water boards' renewal programs and award lists; the competitors' annual reports 2025; the national welding register 2026; the alderpipes.example home page.

market.headline: Seven water boards spend about €1.1 billion a year on pipe renewal, and Westland now tenders large lots.
market.body: Westland spends about a third of the boards' total. Its program for 2027 to 2037 sets lots of €60 million and more. The first three lots open for bids in June 2027.
market.source: Water boards' renewal programs, June 2026; Westland tender notice, October 2026

customers.headline: Westland paid 46% of Alder's revenue in 2025, up from 21% in 2021.
customers.body: The six smaller water boards paid 41% and the two gas network operators 13%. Each board uses the pipes and pays for the work itself. Every award sits on the public tender record.

competitors.headline: Alder is the smallest of the four builders that win most of the boards' pipe work.
competitors.body: Hollis Build had revenue of €920 million in 2025, against Alder's €84m. All four compete for the same lots and the same licensed welders. The floor is a board that delays renewal and repairs old pipe with its own crews.
competitors.source: Competitors' annual reports 2025; national welding register 2026

assets.headline: Alder holds twenty years of acceptance records at every water board.
assets.body: The records let Alder pass the past-performance gate in any tender. It held four open Westland contracts worth €61 million at the end of 2025. Its cash was €7.6 million.

capabilities.headline: Alder delivers lots under €40 million with its own crews, again and again.
capabilities.body: It won 27 lots from 2021 to 2025, every one under €40 million. The smaller boards recorded fewer defects on its sections than their average. It has never led a lot above €38 million.
capabilities.source: Boards' award lists and acceptance reports, 2021 to 2025

limits.headline: Each lot needs a bank guarantee of 10% of its value, and Alder's largest so far was €3.8 million.
limits.body: A €60 million Westland lot needs a €6 million guarantee. Receivables rose from 19% of revenue in 2021 to 31% in 2025, while cash stayed at 9%. The board approves every contract over €5 million.
limits.source: Westland general conditions, 2024; Alder annual report 2025

invests.headline: Alder spent €3 million on a second welding crew in 2025, paid from cash.
invests.body: It won two Westland lots in 2025, worth €19 million together. Its bid list for 2026 holds no lot over €40 million.

cuts.headline: Alder recorded no sale of a unit, no closure and no layoff from 2021 to 2025.
cuts.body: The annual reports for those five years record none.

hires.headline: Alder's staff rose from 330 to 410 between 2021 and 2025.
hires.body: Most of the new staff are welders. They come from the same two training schools that Hollis Build and Carrow Group hire from.
hires.source: Alder annual report 2025; national welding register 2026

story.headline: Alder tells its story as the builder with its own crews, ready for the boards' decade of renewal.
story.body: The annual report calls Alder "the specialist for the boards' renewal decade". The website's first line reads "Our own crews, every metre".

signal.headline: The website shows people at work in trenches, the crews before the projects.
signal.body: The home page opens on a photograph of two welders in a trench. It shows no picture of a finished project.

pulls.title: The guarantee outgrows Alder
pulls.sentence: Westland's new lots start at €60 million and each needs a €6 million guarantee, while the largest guarantee Alder has posted was €3.8 million.
pulls.from_fact: The largest guarantee Alder has posted was €3.8 million
pulls.to_fact: bundles its work into lots of €60 million and more
pulls.who_pays: Alder's owners and staff, if Alder cannot bid on Westland's lots when they open in June 2027.

pulls.title: One buyer, more unpaid work
pulls.sentence: Westland paid 46% of Alder's revenue in 2025, while receivables rose to 31% of revenue and cash stayed at 9%.
pulls.from_fact: Westland paid 46% of Alder's revenue in 2025.
pulls.to_fact: Receivables were 31% of revenue at the end of 2025
pulls.who_pays: Alder, which carries the unpaid work with its own cash and pays its bank a fee on every guarantee.

pulls.title: The same welders
pulls.sentence: Alder grew its staff from 330 to 410, most of them welders, from the same two schools that its larger competitors hire from.
pulls.from_fact: Alder's staff rose from 330 at the end of 2021 to 410 at the end of 2025
pulls.to_fact: hire licensed welders from the same two training schools as Alder
pulls.who_pays: Alder, in wages, if Hollis Build or Carrow Group hire more welders for the 2027 lots. [INFERRED]

decision.what: Whether Alder bids for Westland's first €60 million lots, and how it covers the €6 million guarantee each one needs.
decision.by_when: June 2027, when the first lots open for bids

options.option: Bid in a consortium with a larger builder
options.cost: a share of each lot's margin, to a partner that also competes for Alder's welders.

options.option: Ask Kestrel Bank for a €6 million guarantee
options.cost: a yearly fee for as long as the lot runs, and Alder Holding's approval to put cash at risk beyond one year.

options.option: Keep to lots under €40 million at the smaller boards
options.cost: the Westland work that paid 46% of Alder's revenue in 2025.

decision.if_nobody: Alder's bid list for 2026 holds no lot over €40 million, so the first Westland lots go to the larger builders when the award list comes out in December 2027.
